questions.question: What is the main advantage of WebSockets over HTTP for real-time communication?

options.text: WebSockets maintain a persistent bidirectional connection
WebSockets use less bandwidth for initial connection

questions.explanation: WebSockets establish a persistent, full-duplex connection. Both client and server can send messages anytime without the overhead of establishing new connections. HTTP requires new request for each message.

questions.question: Which use cases are ideal for WebSockets? (Choose all that apply)
questions.explanation: WebSockets excel at real-time, bidirectional communication: chat, gaming, live data feeds. Static content doesn't need real-time updates—standard HTTP with caching is more appropriate.

questions.question: How does a WebSocket connection begin?

options.text: HTTP upgrade request that switches protocol to WebSocket

questions.explanation: WebSocket starts as HTTP request with 'Upgrade: websocket' header. Server responds with 101 Switching Protocols, and the connection upgrades from HTTP to WebSocket protocol over the same TCP connection.

questions.question: What challenge does WebSocket introduce for load balancing?

options.text: Long-lived connections require sticky sessions or connection-aware routing

questions.explanation: WebSocket connections are long-lived and stateful. Simple round-robin doesn't work—messages must route to the server holding the connection. Sticky sessions or connection-aware infrastructure is needed.

questions.question: A WebSocket server needs to broadcast a message to 100,000 connected clients. What is a potential challenge?

options.text: Memory and CPU for maintaining many concurrent connections
Each broadcast requires a new connection

questions.explanation: Each WebSocket connection consumes server memory (buffers, state). 100K connections require significant resources. Broadcasting to all also requires iterating through connections. Horizontal scaling and pub/sub help.

questions.question: What happens when a WebSocket connection is interrupted?

options.text: The connection is lost; client must implement reconnection logic
The server maintains the session indefinitely

questions.explanation: WebSocket doesn't have built-in reconnection. When connection drops, it's gone. Clients must implement reconnection logic, and applications must handle message loss during disconnection.

questions.question: True or False: WebSockets are always better than HTTP polling for real-time updates.
questions.explanation: WebSockets add complexity (connection management, scaling). For infrequent updates or simple use cases, long-polling or SSE may be simpler. WebSockets shine for high-frequency, bidirectional communication.

questions.question: How can WebSocket servers be scaled horizontally?

options.text: Using a pub/sub system (Redis) to coordinate messages across server instances

questions.explanation: With multiple servers, a client connected to Server A needs messages from Server B. A pub/sub backbone (Redis, Kafka) distributes messages to all servers, which then push to their connected clients.

questions.question: What is the WebSocket frame format used for?

options.text: Structuring messages with opcode, length, and payload

questions.explanation: WebSocket frames contain: opcode (text/binary/close/ping/pong), payload length, masking key (client→server), and payload data. This lightweight framing enables efficient message transmission.

questions.question: Which protocol provides server-to-client push without bidirectional communication?
questions.explanation: SSE is unidirectional (server→client only) over HTTP. It's simpler than WebSocket when you only need server push (live feeds, notifications). WebSocket is needed for bidirectional communication.

questions.question: A chat application uses WebSockets. How should it handle user authentication?

options.text: Authentication is not needed for WebSockets
Authenticate during HTTP upgrade or send auth token as first message
Use a separate HTTP endpoint only

questions.explanation: WebSocket doesn't have built-in auth. Common approaches: authenticate during upgrade handshake (cookies, tokens in query string) or require auth message immediately after connection before accepting other messages.

questions.question: What is a WebSocket 'heartbeat' or 'ping/pong' mechanism?

options.text: A way to measure server CPU
Periodic messages to detect dead connections and keep connection alive

questions.explanation: Heartbeats (ping/pong frames) detect dead connections that didn't close cleanly and keep connections alive through proxies/firewalls that might timeout idle connections. Essential for connection health.
